exploration.title: Pollinator Express
exploration.subject: Biology
exploration.summary: Predict, trace and compare when one modeled bee visit transfers compatible pollen.
exploration.question: What can flower visits tell us about pollen transfer—and what can they not tell us?
exploration.explanation: Pollinators often visit flowers for nectar or pollen and may move pollen to a flower’s receptive part. That transfer is pollination. Fertilization can happen later after pollen-tube growth and the joining of sperm and egg cells; seed dispersal later moves formed seeds. This deterministic lesson records only pollen transfer. First it changes only the displayed type of one trial flower at one fixed position. Then it changes only whether one bridge habitat patch containing a Gold and a Violet flower is present; the same planned route uses the Gold bridge stop in both conditions. Every coordinate, reach value, flower placement and route is invented for teaching, not an ecological measurement, probability or forecast. Real plants vary in compatibility and self-pollination, and real pollinators can carry mixed pollen.

experiments.title: Change only the trial flower type
experiments.instruction: Predict first. Compare Gold 1 followed by the fixed trial flower set to Gold type with the same route and position set to Violet type. Reach, habitat, coordinates and transfer rule stay fixed.
experiments.observe: Both routes record two visits. Compare one compatible transfer with zero and explain why a visit count alone does not establish compatible pollen transfer.

experiments.title: Bridge a habitat gap
experiments.instruction: Predict first. Attempt the same Gold 1 → Gold 2 → Gold bridge → Gold 3 route at reach 170 with a bridge habitat patch absent and present. The patch contains a Gold and a Violet flower, but the fixed planned route uses only the Gold bridge stop. Only patch presence changes.
experiments.observe: Without the patch, the Gold bridge and Gold 3 attempts are blocked. With it, both succeed. Explain how the Gold stop in the added modeled patch changes route connectivity without treating the result as an ecological forecast.

exploration.misconception: A flower visit is not automatically pollination; pollination is not fertilization; and a received-pollen mark does not mean that fruit or seeds formed or dispersed.
